# Evaluation of the Double Integral

We wish to compute
$$I = \int_0^\infty \int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-x-y}}{x+y}\,dx\,dy.$$

## Step 1: Change of variables

Let $u = x+y$ and $v = x/(x+y)$, so that $x = uv$ and $y = u(1-v)$. The Jacobian is
$$\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right| = \begin{vmatrix} v & u \\ 1-v & -u \end{vmatrix} = -uv - u(1-v) = -u,$$
so $|J| = u$.

The first quadrant $x\ge 0,\, y\ge 0$ maps to $u \in [0,\infty)$, $v \in [0,1]$. The integrand becomes
$$\frac{e^{-x-y}}{x+y} = \frac{e^{-u}}{u},$$
and with the Jacobian factor $u$, the integral transforms to
$$I = \int_0^\infty \int_0^1 \frac{e^{-u}}{u}\cdot u\,dv\,du = \int_0^\infty e^{-u}\left(\int_0^1 dv\right)du = \int_0^\infty e^{-u}\,du.$$

## Step 2: Evaluate

$$I = \int_0^\infty e^{-u}\,du = \left[-e^{-u}\right]_0^\infty = 0 - (-1) = 1.$$

## Verification (alternative approach)

Using the identity $\dfrac{1}{x+y} = \displaystyle\int_0^\infty e^{-(x+y)t}\,dt$ for $x+y>0$:

$$I = \int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty e^{-x-y}\int_0^\infty e^{-(x+y)t}\,dt\,dx\,dy = \int_0^\infty \left(\int_0^\infty e^{-x(1+t)}dx\right)\left(\int_0^\infty e^{-y(1+t)}dy\right)dt.$$

Each inner integral equals $\dfrac{1}{1+t}$, so
$$I = \int_0^\infty \frac{dt}{(1+t)^2} = \left[-\frac{1}{1+t}\right]_0^\infty = 1.$$

Both methods agree.

## Result

$$\boxed{\int_0^\infty \int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-x-y}}{x+y}\,dx\,dy = 1}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
